Inglewood, California
  June 25, 2019

The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a special meeting on
Tuesday, June 25, 2019, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.
Mayor Butts called the City Council into session for Closed Session at the hour of
1:01 p.m.

The City Clerk announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor Butts, Council Members Dotson, Padilla,
  Morales, and Franklin; and
  Absent:  None.

City officials and personnel present for Closed Session were as follows:

  Yvonne Horton  City Clerk
  Artie Fields  City Manager
  Aisha Thompson  Deputy City Clerk

PUBLIC COMMENTS REGARDING CLOSED SESSION ITEMS. Mayor
Butts inquired if there were any persons present who wished to address the City
Council on the Closed Session Item.

There was no response.

Mayor Butts recessed the City Council at the hour of 1:01 p.m. for Closed Session
Item No. CS-1.

  *****************

Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called
the City Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, Housing
Authority, and Finance Authority, at the hour of 2:01 p.m.
The City Clerk/ Successor Agency Secretary/ Housing Authority
Secretary/Finance Authority Secretary announced the presence of a quorum as

  Authority Chairman/Finance Authority Chairman
  Butts, Council Members/Successor Agency

  Authority Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales and
  Franklin; and
  Absent:  None.

personnel present were as follows:
  Yvonne Horton  City Clerk/Secretary*

  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  David Esparza  Asst. City Manager/CFO

Authority.

 127.2  COUNCIL INITIATIVE

  Mayor Butts:

  Initiative by Mayor James T. Butts, Jr., recommending adoption of Ordinance No.
  19-13 to amend Chapter 8 (Business, Trades, and Professions) of the Inglewood
  Municipal Code to add a new Article 9 (Housing Protection Initiative) for the
  regulation of rent increases and just cause evictions for certain covered residential
  rental units.

  MAYOR BUTTS COMMENTS:

  Mayor Butts inquired with the City Attorney how long the Moratorium was
  extended.

  Ken Campos, City Attorney, stated until December 15, 2019, 180 days.

  Mayor Butts commented that he is going to pull Agenda Item No. CI-1, and bring
  it back for modifications for the 1st reading, and subsequent 2nd reading. He stated
  he’s pulling the item because he’s been in communication with apartment owners,
  and tenants, and he’s come to the conclusion that the Council has come to a
  fantastic balance between Landlords and tenants. He also stated that the
  Council’s intent is to allow people who have lived in the City of Inglewood for
  decades an opportunity to experience the new Inglewood.

  Mayor Butts stated that an annual increase of 5%, will compute to a 25% increase
  in five years, if a landlord chooses to do so. He stated in California, people spend
  on an average 35% to 45% of their income on housing cost. He also stated that a
  truly fair initiative is not to control rent but to protect people’s ability to afford the
  new Inglewood. He also stated that in 6 years, 12,000 jobs will be online for the
  stadium development, and by that time it will be difficult for anybody to live in
  the City of Inglewood, with that type of increase. Mayor Butts commented that
  the Ordinance needs tier increases, and engage in proactive employment
  development strategies to provide training opportunities targeted at apartment
  owners that are low income. He also stated that he believes that the City Council
  has a moral responsibility to provide [the word social justice word is used and
  there is never any operation reality put to it and it’s just a concept]. He stated he
  feels the City Council needs to put in place strategies that will enable people and
  not just survive, but to thrive in the new Inglewood. Finally, he stated that he
  wants to pull Agenda Item No. CI-1, and bring it with some amendments to be
  discussed by the City Council.

  Ken Campos, City Attorney inquired if the Mayor was requesting a motion to pull
  the item.

  Mayor Butts affirmed.

  It was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council Member Dotson that the
  City Council does hereby pull the Mayor’s initiative from the Agenda. The
  motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.
